summary: Revision 2 extends revision 1's explorer and shortcut registry instead of adding parallel ones. R13 adds a 'home' source to the pure explorerRoot() in src/features/explorer/root.ts plus an optional homeFolder argument; App fetches that path once through one new thin explorer_home command (USERPROFILE, the same lookup themes_cmds.rs already uses) and a typed explorerApi.home() wrapper, so when no app root applies (home view, editor with no tab or an unsaved tab) the panel roots at the user's home folder. useExplorer's existing Up machinery, already used by Misc roots, is allowed for home roots too, so Up climbs one folder at a time and from a drive reaches the existing explorer_drives list. Home listing reuses the one-level lister and the 100-level LRU cache, so browsing huge trees stays bounded; no tab code is touched anywhere on the root path, so a root change cannot close or alter a tab. This supersedes revision 1's A5 'home has no root' hint, which now only appears if the core cannot report a home folder. R6 turns the shared registry's F5 entry into a toggleApp id (every F5 variant maps to it, so F5 never means refresh), drops refresh's key, and keeps App's single global key listener registered once: the handler calls a live toggleApp closure through a ref, and toggleApp reads view, app and states at press time, computes appButton(app.terminals.map(stateOf)) exactly as AppHeader does, then calls the same startAll / stopAll the on-screen button calls (no terminals or a non-app view means no-op, and preventDefault keeps F5 a true no-op outside the app view). Runtime's existing transition guard already makes a repeated start a no-op, so rapid F5 presses cannot start a second copy; the work is O(terminals) with no disk, network or polling. R7 removes the finder's min(640px, 80vw) demand and makes it fill and wrap inside its container, so it fits the shared dialog now and a side pane later at desktop and 360px widths; the fix is CSS only. R8 adds one small adapter, SidePane, over the approved jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout 2.8.0 (verified: ISC, peer React ^18.2 with 18.3.1 installed, no runtime deps, ~12 kB JS, and its published ESM bundle injects its own stylesheet at import time, so the earlier missing-CSS rejection does not apply). Dialog keeps its exact props/actions API and renders its body and actions inside the adapter's pane; BranchMenu uses the same adapter. The pane's named close control and Escape both run the dialog's cancel action, which defaults to the last action, so every existing dialog keeps its content, fields, buttons, actions and close paths; the only added affordance is the named keyboard close that the accessibility requirement mandates, and the desktop overlay dims without adding a click-to-dismiss path (today's dialog backdrop does not close on a click). This is the supersession recorded in R8 (analyst-r4) of 20261125-153618:R2's 'no existing dialog is redesigned or replaced' clause for dialog presentation only; R2's promise that every existing screen, panel, dialog and the footer remains present still holds, and the command palette stays a palette. Each pane is a fixed overlay, so only the open pane mounts; the package is imported only by the adapter/Dialog/BranchMenu, and if the package proves unusable R8 stops while R13, R6 and R7 still ship. No new capability permission or CSP change is needed: explorer_home only reads USERPROFILE, and the existing explorer_list/explorer_drives already accept any absolute path.

additions.title: Ask the core for the user's home folder
additions.why: The home view and an editor with no file have to show the person's home folder, and the window must not guess or hard-code a Windows path.
acceptance: In the home view, or in the editor with no tab open or an unsaved tab, the explorer's top folder is the same folder Windows calls the user's home folder.
The home path comes from one typed src/api function backed by one thin Tauri command; no home path is written anywhere in the window code.

The command reads only USERPROFILE and does no disk scan, so it costs nothing on startup; when the core cannot determine a home folder no listing request is made and the panel falls back to its existing no-root hint instead of an error.

additions.title: Add the approved responsive-layout package and prove it is usable
additions.why: R8 names the jattac responsive-layout library as the source of the side panes, and an earlier jattac package had to be rejected because its published build shipped no CSS.
acceptance: npm install succeeds with jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout ^2.8.0 alongside React 18.3.1 with no peer-dependency error, and package.json plus package-lock.json record it.
A pane rendered by the adapter is styled without any separate CSS import, because the published 2.8.0 ESM bundle injects its own stylesheet on import.
The lockfile records the exact published 2.8.0 version, and the dependency is named with its reason in the design.

additions.title: Keep focus, Escape and cancel behaviour when dialogs move to the pane
additions.why: Moving confirmations into a side pane must not make a destructive dialog easier to misfire or impossible to dismiss from the keyboard.
acceptance: Opening a dialog still focuses its first (default) action and exposes exactly one role=dialog named by its title.

The pane's close control has an accessible name and, together with Escape, runs the dialog's cancel action, which defaults to its last action and is never the destructive one; the desktop overlay dims but does not close, matching today's dialog backdrop, and a dialog with no actions (update downloading or installing) has no close path at all.

Every existing confirmation flow (stop-and-save, delete app, close console, switch branch, restore, quit, update, help, theme finder) still completes or cancels through the same buttons and keeps its content, fields, buttons and actions; the recorded R8 supersession of 20261125-153618:R2 covers presentation only, so every dialog is still present.

additions.title: Pin the current dialog and branch menu behaviour before changing them
additions.why: The shared Dialog and BranchMenu were already shipped, so their current behaviour has to be frozen by tests before their shell is replaced (USR-004).
acceptance: Before any production edit, the existing Dialog and BranchMenu tests are run and extended to pin first-action focus, role and accessible name, per-action callbacks, branch filtering and picking, loading text, and Escape closing.

After the pane change those same behaviours pass, with only the deliberately changed presentation (side pane instead of centred modal, plus the accessibility-mandated named close control) asserted differently.
